extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / readers of IUT (inter-universal Teichmüller theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Survey-style presentation of definitions, constructions, and examples of Frobenioids (elementary, model, tempered, p-adic, Archimedean, global), auxiliary notions (splittings, Kummer structures, birationalisation, realification, primes of monoids), and the reconstruction theorem from Frobenioids to mono-theta environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual characterization of Frobenioids
rubrics_metrics.description: Anabelioid (=Galois category) : Frobenioid = coverings : line bundles over coverings — the theory of Frobenioids is a categorical formulation of line bundles over coverings (formulated purely categorically; geometric terms need not appear).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This positions Frobenioids as categorical analogues of the classical geometry of line bundles on covers; Mochizuki's general theory [FrdI, FrdII] develops this, but the survey focuses on model Frobenioids used in IUT. Main theorems are category-theoretic reconstruction algorithms of related objects, though the survey often includes the objects to be reconstructed as input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary Frobenioid (Definition 8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a category D and a contravariant functor θ: D → Mon (a monoid on D), define the category F(θ) with Ob(F(θ)) = Ob(D) and, for A,B in Ob(D), Hom_F(θ)(A,B) consisting of triples φ = (Base(φ); Div(φ); degFr(φ)) ∈ Hom_D(A,B) × θ(A) × N_{>0}. Composition is given by Base of composites, Div composed with action and scaled by degFr, and multiplication of degFr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a natural functor F(θ) → D sending objects and Base(φ). If θ(A) is group-like (all elements invertible) for every A, θ is called group-like. An elementary Frobenioid is the category F(θ) associated to θ. The notion of pre-Frobenioid (a covariant functor C → F(θ)) and the induced operations Base, Div, degFr on C are introduced; technical conditions turn a pre-Frobenioid into a Frobenioid (not recalled here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Frobenioid and induced structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A covariant functor C → F(θ) (for some elementary Frobenioid F(θ)) is called a pre-Frobenioid structure on C; a category C equipped with such a functor is a pre-Frobenioid. From the functor one obtains Base(), Div(), degFr() operations on objects/morphisms of C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation for automorphisms/endormorphisms with Base = id and degFr = 1: O^2(A) ⊆ Aut_C(A), O^3(A) ⊆ End_C(A). Also defines O^2(A)_{N} = {a in O^2(A) | a^N = 1}. When pre-Frobenioids satisfy additional technical conditions they are Frobenioids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Split pre-Frobenioid ((N)-split) (Definition 8.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there exists a functorial splitting spl: O^3/O^2 → O^3 (resp. a Z_N-orbit of such splittings) of the quotient O^3(A)/O^2(A) for all A and morphisms with degFr = 1, then the pair (C, spl) is a split pre-Frobenioid (resp. a N-split pre-Frobenioid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Splittings are required to be functorial in A and respect morphisms of degFr = 1. The splitting data refines the pre-Frobenioid structure and is used in constructions and reconstructions (e.g., in examples such as p-adic Frobenioids where canonical splittings occur).

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism notion for pre-Frobenioids
rubrics_metrics.description: Isomorphisms between pre-Frobenioids are not mere category equivalences but equivalences that include the pre-Frobenioid structures: for pre-Frobenioids F → F(θ), F' → F(θ') (with θ on D and θ' on D'), an isomorphism consists of equivalence classes of category equivalences F' ≃ F, D' ≃ D, and a natural transformation θ' → θ|_{D'} making the induced square between F(θ') and F(θ) 1-commutative (one composite is isomorphic to the other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This strengthens the usual notion of equivalence by requiring compatibility with divisor-monoid structures; see [IUTchI, Remark 3.2.1(ii)].

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Frobenioid (Definition 8.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given θ: D → Mon, a group-like monoid B: D → Mon and a homomorphism Div_B : B → θ^{gp}, write θ^{birat} = Im(Div_B) ⊆ θ^{gp}. The model Frobenioid C has objects pairs A = (A_D, α) with A_D ∈ Ob(D) and α ∈ θ(A_D)^{gp}. Morphisms from A to B are quadruples φ = (Base(φ), Div(φ), degFr(φ), u(φ)) ∈ Hom_D(A_D,B_D) × θ(A) × N_{>0} × B(A) satisfying degFr(φ)(α_A) + Div(φ) = θ(Base(φ))(α_B) + Div_B(u(φ)). Composition is given by explicit formulas combining Base, Div, degFr and u via B(Base) and degFr scaling. The category C is equipped with a pre-Frobenioid structure C → F(θ) by projecting to Base and (Base,Div,degFr).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C is called the model Frobenioid defined by divisor monoid θ and rational function monoid B. Under additional conditions the model Frobenioid is a Frobenioid. This construction realizes line-bundle-like objects categorically via the extra data α and u.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trivial line bundle in a model Frobenioid (Definition 8.4 (1))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a model Frobenioid F with base category D, the trivial line bundle OA over A in Ob(D) is the object determined by (A; 0) ∈ Ob(D) × θ(A)^{gp}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These trivial objects (called Frobenius-trivial in [FrdI]) can under some conditions be reconstructed category-theoretically from F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Birationalisation of a model Frobenioid (Definition 8.4 (2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a model Frobenioid C, define C^{birat} to have the same objects as C but morphisms Hom_{C^{birat}}(A,B) = colim_{A'→A, Base(isom), degFr=1} Hom_C(A',B) (direct limit over isomorphisms of bases with degFr=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The birationalisation simplifies morphisms by allowing birational base changes. For general Frobenioids the definition is more complicated; there is a natural functor C → C^{birat}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realification (realićation) of a model Frobenioid (Definition 8.4 (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a model Frobenioid with divisor monoid θ and rational function monoid B, form θ_R := θ ⊗_Z Z_{(0)}^{R_0} (notation in text) and B_R := R ⋅ Im(B → θ^{gp}) ⊆ (θ_R)^{gp}. The realified model Frobenioid C_R is obtained by replacing θ by θ_R and B by B_R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This construction enlarges divisor monoids and rational function monoids (e.g., to include real coefficients) and yields a natural functor C → C_R. Additional conditions may be needed to include more model Frobenioids not treated in the survey.

rubrics_metrics.name: ((2)-, (2)(N)-) Kummer structure on a pre-Frobenioid (Definition 8.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a topological group G isomorphic to the absolute Galois group of an MLF, one reconstructs an ind-topological monoid G ⋉ O^3(G) with G-action; write O^2(G) := (O^3(G))^{(2)} and related torsion quotients. Define Isomet(G) as the group of G-equivariant isometries of O^2(O^22)(G) preserving integral structures. For a pre-Frobenioid C with base D equivalent to connected finite étale coverings of an MLF or CAF and a universal covering pro-object A1 with G = Aut(A1), a (2)-Kummer structure on C is a bZ(2)-orbit of isomorphisms O^2(G)_{/…} → O^2(A1) of ind-topological G-modules (resp. an Isomet-orbit for the (2)(22)-case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These Kummer structures are independent of the choice of A1; (2)-Kummer structures on C are unique up to the stated automorphisms. A pre-Frobenioid equipped with such structure is a (2)-Kummer pre-Frobenioid; if also split, one obtains split-(2)-Kummer pre-Frobenioid. Remark 8.5.1 notes that automorphisms induced by Aut(G) cannot equal those from Isomet(G) with nontrivial image in Z_p due to compatibility with the p-adic logarithm of the cyclotomic character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric Frobenioid example (Example 8.6)
rubrics_metrics.description:
Given a proper normal geometrically integral variety V over a field k with function field k(V) and a (possibly infinite) Galois extension k(V)^{#}, let G = Gal(k(V)^{#}/k(V)) and D_{k(V)} a set of Q-Cartier prime divisors on V. For each finite extension L of k(V) inside k(V)^{#}, define θ(L) = Z_{
eq 0}[D_L] (monoid of effective Cartier divisors supported on D_L) and B(L) = L^× with poles/zeros supported in D_L; the functorial data determine a model Frobenioid C_{V;k(V)^{#};D_k(V)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objects correspond to line bundles representable by Cartier divisors with support in D_L; morphisms correspond to base morphisms, a degree d ∈ N_{>0}, and maps of line bundles with zero locus a Cartier divisor supported in D_L. This illustrates the geometric origins of model Frobenioids.

rubrics_metrics.name: p-adic Frobenioid construction (Example 8.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite extension K_v of Q_p and certain categories D_v and D'_v of finite étale coverings (built from an arithmetic curve X → v and its local structures), one constructs monoids θ_{C_v} and θ_{C'_v} (via ord(O^3_{?}) perfections) and rational-function-like monoids B — these determine p-adic pre-Frobenioids (in fact p-adic Frobenioids) called C_v and C'_v. There are canonical splittings spl'_v coming from certain elements like the normalized theta function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The construction uses left-adjoints between covering categories and the perfection functor; these p-adic Frobenioids serve as local building blocks in IUT applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Div+ (effective Cartier log-divisors) and Mero (log-meromorphic functions) (Definition 8.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a stable formal model Z_1 of a tempered covering, Div+(Z_1) is the monoid of effective Cartier divisors whose support lies in the union of the special fiber and cusps of Z_1 (called effective Cartier log-divisors). Mero(Z_1) is the group of meromorphic functions f on Z_1 such that for any N≥1, f admits an N-th root over some tempered covering of Z (called log-meromorphic functions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notions are used in tempered Frobenioid constructions to capture divisors and meromorphic-type functions adapted to the tempered/analytic setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tempered filter and tempered Frobenioid construction (Definition 8.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: A tempered filtration {I_i}_{i∈I} of a tempered group Π_temp is a filtration by characteristic open subgroups satisfying (a) intersection is trivial, (b) each I_i admits an open characteristic subgroup I_i^1 such that I_i/I_i^1 is free and for any open normal H⊆I_i with free quotient there exists I_i^1 with containment properties, and (c) for each open H⊆Π there is a unique I_i^1_H etc. Given such a filtration and split stable reductions for coverings, one defines functors θ^0, B^0 from categories of tempered coverings to monoids by limits over Div+ and Mero invariants; restricting/building constant subfunctors and realifications yields model Frobenioids F_v and C_v (tempered and base-field-theoretic hull respectively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parts (2) and (3) of the definition explain how to produce θ^0 and B^0 by inverse limits over Gal-actions on Div+ and Mero of stable models, how to obtain subcategories Dell and left adjoints, and how to form realified monoids θ_R and B_R. These yield tempered Frobenioids used in analytic/tempered parts of IUT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tempered Frobenioid features and constructions (Example 8.8 continued)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tempered Frobenioids come with specific elements (e.g., normalized theta function roots q_v and their logarithms) that generate submonoids, give split pre-Frobenioids, and allow formation of p-adic or analytic sub-Frobenioids (C'_v, C_v etc). There are inclusions of base-field-theoretic hulls into full Frobenioids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tempered constructions are tailored to hyperbolic curves of specified types; they provide the analytic input needed for constructing mono-theta environments and for cyclotomic rigidity phenomena referenced later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archimedean Frobenioid (Example 8.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an Archimedean local field K_v ≅ C, define a category C_v whose objects are pairs (V,A) where V is a one-dimensional K_v-vector space and A ⊂ V is an 'angular region' (connected open subset of S^1 or interval in R_{>0} per the ord(O^3) identification). Morphisms consist of degFr ∈ N_{>0} and vector-space isomorphisms V^{⊗degFr} → V' sending A^{⊗degFr} into A'; Div(φ) := log(λ) for the maximal λ>0 with λ·Im(A^{⊗degFr}) ⊆ A' giving a real-valued divisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The triple (C_v; D_v; ν_v) with appropriate monoid functor yields an Archimedean Frobenioid, representing Archimedean arithmetic-line-bundle data. There are natural isomorphisms of topological monoids O^3(C_v) ≅ ord(O^3_{K_v}) etc., and canonical splittings leading to split-Frobenioids C'_v used in analytic parts of IUT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global realiśed Frobenioid (Example 8.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a number field F_mod, form the monoid θ_mod(F_mod) = ⊕_{v∈V_non} ord(O^3_v) ⊕_{v∈V_arc} ord(O^3_v) where ord(O^3_v) = Z_{≥0} for non-archimedean v and R_{≥0} for archimedean v. Elements are effective arithmetic divisors; B(F_mod) = F_mod^× maps to θ_mod(F_mod)^{gp} by f ↦ (f)_0 - (f)_∞. The data (Spec F_mod; θ_mod; B) determine the global realiﬁed model Frobenioid C_mod.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ties together local contributions into a global Frobenioid capturing arithmetic divisors and rational functions globally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primes of a commutative monoid (Definition 8.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a commutative monoid M with 0 the only invertible element, injective M → M^{gp}, and the condition that a∈M^{gp} with n·a∈M for some n>0 lies in image(M), define relations: (1) a ≼ b if ∃c∈M with a + c = b; (2) a ≺ b if ∃n≥1 with a ≼ n·b; (3) a ≠ 0 is primary if for any b with M ∋ b ≺ a implies b ≼ a; (4) the relation a ≺ b is an equivalence among primary elements and equivalence classes are called primes of M. Prime(M) denotes the set of these primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notion of primes differs from usual monoid primes; it is used to define Prime(θ_mod) and to index local components (e.g., places v) in global constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic rigidity and reconstruction to mono-theta environments (Theorem 8.14 and surrounding discussion)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a category-theoretic algorithm that reconstructs a (mod N) mono-theta environment M(F_v) from a tempered Frobenioid F_v. Corollary 7.22 reconstructs mono-theta environments from topological groups; combined with Theorem 8.14 these relate group-theoretic and Frobenioid-theoretic constructions via mono-theta environments and Kummer theory (using cyclotomic rigidity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The construction produces triples M(F_v) = (E_N; D_F; s_F^{(2)}) encoding mod-N mono-theta data (E_N a subgroup, DF a subgroup generated by outer actions, s_F a cohomology class). References: [EtTh, Theorem 5.10], [IUTchII, Proposition 1.2(ii)]. This is the core reconstruction link used in later Hodge-Arakelov evaluation map constructions (Section 11.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Group/cohomological constructions in the passage F_v → M(F_v) (Subsection 8.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given tempered Frobenioid data (theta-trivial objects, l-th roots of theta functions, groups H(...) arising from automorphism images, and actions on sections and theta-trivialisations), one forms homomorphisms u-gp_N and t-gp_N from H(...) into automorphism groups; the cocycle differences of These actions give cohomology classes equal to Kummer classes of l-th roots and mod-N Kummer classes, and one obtains subgroups EN, outer actions by K_2, and the triple M(F_v) = (E_N; DF; s_F^{(2)}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although many details are omitted in the survey, the paragraph explains how algebraic/analytic theta-data and automorphism groups yield cohomological Kummer classes and group-theoretic data that assemble into a mono-theta environment; references include [EtTh, Proposition 5.2], [EtTh, Theorem 5.6, 5.7].
